title: Affine square-zero lifting criterion for a stack smooth over a scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $p:\mathcal X\to S$ an algebraic stack [def-pc-scheme, def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Assume $p$ is locally of finite presentation, meaning that a smooth surjective scheme atlas has locally finitely presented structural composite [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose that, for every first order thickening $i:T\hookrightarrow T\prime$ of affine $S$-schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], the restriction functor $i^*:\mathcal X(T\prime)\to\mathcal X(T)$ is essentially surjective: for every $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ there exist $x\prime\in\mathcal X(T\prime)$ and an isomorphism $i^*x\prime\cong x$ over $T$. Then $p$ is smooth: there exists a smooth surjective scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X$ with smooth composite $U\to S$.

source.place: Tags 0DP0, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth, and 0DNY, lemma-reformulate-formal-smoothness; target the representable stack S.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $a:U\to\mathcal X$ for which $b=p\circ a:U\to S$ is locally of finite presentation; this is the atlas supplied by the hypothesis. The atlas terminology is [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. To prove $b$ formally smooth in [def-sbc-formally-smooth], fix any affine first order thickening $i:T\hookrightarrow T^{\prime}$ over $S$ and any $u:T\to U$ over $S$.

source.place: Tag 0DP0, converse: choose a smooth scheme atlas and test its structural composite

proof.text: Apply the assumed essential surjectivity to $x=a\circ u\in\mathcal X(T)$. Obtain $x^{\prime}\in\mathcal X(T^{\prime})$ and $\alpha:i^*x^{\prime}\xrightarrow{\sim}a\circ u$. By the atlas definition [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], $Z=T^{\prime}\times_{\mathcal X}U$ is an algebraic space and its projection $q:Z\to T^{\prime}$ is smooth. In the explicit 2-fibre product of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], the triple $(i,u,\alpha)$ defines a morphism $s:T\to Z$ with $qs=i$ and $\operatorname{pr}_U s=u$. Here $Z$ is the pullback along the chosen object $x^{\prime}$, so the isomorphism $\alpha$ is retained.

source.place: Tags 0DP0 and 0DNY: composition of object lifts with the atlas, expanded as a 2-fibre product

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-affine-infinitesimal-lift] to the smooth algebraic-space map $q:Z\to T^{\prime}$, the same affine first order thickening $i$, the map $s$, and $\mathrm{id}_{T^{\prime}}$. It gives $s^{\prime}:T^{\prime}\to Z$ with $qs^{\prime}=\mathrm{id}_{T^{\prime}}$ and $s^{\prime}i=s$. Put $u^{\prime}=\operatorname{pr}_U s^{\prime}$. Then $u^{\prime}i=\operatorname{pr}_U s=u$, and $bu^{\prime}$ is the given structural map $T^{\prime}\to S$, since both projections from $Z$ are over $S$. Thus every test for $b$ lifts, so $b$ is formally smooth [def-sbc-formally-smooth].

source.place: Tag 04AM (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth), smooth implies formal smoothness; applied to the base-changed atlas in the converse of Tag 0DP0

proof.text: The morphism $b$ is locally of finite presentation by its choice in step 1 and formally smooth by step 3. Hence $b$ is smooth by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], whose scheme lifting characterization is Stacks Tag 02H6. The atlas $a$ is still smooth and surjective, and its composite $b$ is smooth. This is exactly smoothness of $p$ in [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack].

source.place: Tag 0DP0, final sentence; more-morphisms.tex Tag 02H6 and stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 075U

Step 2: essential surjectivity gives x' and alpha; the triple (i, u, alpha) is an object of the 2-fibre product Z = T' x_X U. Step 4: b is lfp and formally smooth, so it is smooth and p is smooth by definition.
